title: Card delivery tracking
text: You can check the delivery status of a fictional card with its CARD- id. The demo statuses are delivered, in_transit, and not_shipped. A card that is still in transit cannot be activated yet.

title: Activating a new card
text: A new fictional card starts inactive. Activation is a sensitive action, so the assistant must show the card id and ask for explicit confirmation before changing the status to active.

title: Activation security check
text: The demo never asks for a real PIN, password, full card number, or identity document. Only fictional CARD- ids are accepted. A card owned by another demo customer is rejected by the tool layer.

title: Card not working
text: If a fictional card is not working, the assistant can create a normal-priority ticket. It must not invent a replacement card, a refund, or a delivery date. A human specialist reviews the ticket.

title: Lost or stolen card
text: For a lost or stolen fictional card, the assistant creates a high-priority human handoff ticket. The demo does not perform a real block, replacement, or account closure.

title: Card replacement
text: Card replacement is outside the automated demo. The assistant records the request in a ticket and explains that a human specialist must verify eligibility and delivery details.

title: Changing a card PIN
text: PIN changes are not executed by this demo. The assistant explains the limitation, does not ask for a PIN, and creates a human handoff ticket if the user needs help.

title: Transfer status
text: A fictional transfer is identified by a TXN- id. The demo statuses are pending, completed, failed, and cancelled. The assistant reads the status from the local SQLite database and does not guess.

title: Transfer timing
text: A pending transfer has not completed yet. The demo does not promise a real arrival time. It reports the stored status and creates a ticket if the user needs an investigation.

title: Transfer not received
text: If a fictional recipient has not received a transfer, the assistant first checks the transfer status by TXN- id. A completed transfer can still be investigated through a ticket; the demo does not move money.

title: Cancelling a pending transfer
text: Only a pending fictional transfer can be cancelled. The assistant shows the transfer id, amount, and recipient, then asks for explicit confirmation. The SQLite status changes to cancelled only after confirmation.

title: Cancellation cut-off
text: The demo has no real cut-off clock. A completed, failed, or already cancelled transfer cannot be cancelled again. The assistant reports the current status rather than repeating the action.

title: Transfer fees
text: The fictional demo does not calculate real transfer fees. Any fee statement is a policy example, not a quote. For a concrete fee dispute, the assistant creates a ticket for a human.

title: Top-up methods
text: The demo may describe top-up by bank transfer or card as fictional examples. It does not initiate a real top-up or collect real payment credentials. The available methods are illustrative only.

title: Pending top-up
text: A pending fictional top-up has not been posted to the demo balance. The assistant explains that status and offers a ticket if the user wants the case reviewed.

title: Failed top-up
text: A failed fictional top-up did not change the demo balance. The assistant must not claim that money was credited. It can create a ticket with the fictional reference.

title: Cash withdrawal status
text: Cash withdrawal records are fictional. The assistant can explain the status shown in the demo database, but it cannot reverse a withdrawal or promise a refund.

title: Declined cash withdrawal
text: A declined fictional withdrawal is not a real bank decision. The demo can log the user's concern and hand off to a human; it must not invent a reason or a guaranteed reversal.

title: Exchange rates
text: Exchange rates in the demo are illustrative and not live market quotes. The assistant must not give a real FX recommendation or promise a specific converted amount.

title: Card payment fee
text: A card payment fee shown in the demo is a fictional example. The assistant can explain the record and create a dispute ticket, but it cannot waive a real fee.

title: Unrecognised card payment
text: For an unrecognised fictional card payment, the assistant collects the TXN- id, explains the demo dispute process, and creates a dispute record. It does not issue a provisional credit.

title: Dispute process
text: The demo dispute flow is: identify the transaction, record a reason, create a dispute record, and hand the case to a human reviewer. No real money is moved and no outcome is guaranteed.

title: Dispute timelines
text: The demo does not have real dispute timelines or regulatory deadlines. Any timeline shown is a fictional teaching example. The assistant should say that a human specialist will review the case.

title: Refund status
text: Refund records in this demo are illustrative. The assistant can check a fictional transfer or payment record and create a ticket, but it cannot promise a refund date or amount.

title: Account balance
text: The demo may show a fictional balance summary, but it is not a real account statement. The assistant must not claim that a balance is final or that a pending item has posted.

title: Beneficiary checks
text: A beneficiary name in the demo is fictional. The assistant must not claim to verify a real beneficiary or guarantee that a transfer reached the intended person.

title: Spending and transfer limits
text: Limit information in the demo is a fictional policy example, not a personalised limit. The assistant must not approve an exception or increase a limit automatically.

title: Identity verification
text: The demo does not perform real identity verification and never asks for a password, PIN, full card number, or government id. A request that needs identity checks goes to a human ticket.

title: Human handoff
text: A human handoff creates a high-priority fictional ticket. The assistant explains why it is escalating and does not pretend that a human has already joined the chat.

title: Complaints and security reports
text: Complaints, suspected fraud, and security reports are logged as high-priority tickets. The demo does not block a real card or contact real authorities; it only records the fictional case.
